engagement.title: Cloud Security Assessment
engagement.roe: Testing window 08:00–18:00 CET on business days. No denial-of-service. No data exfiltration beyond proof-of-access sampling. Production write actions require per-operation approval.

executive_summary:
The assessment identified control gaps that, chained together, allowed escalation from a low-privileged identity to organisation-wide administrative access. The most material issues are a permissive S3 public-access configuration and an IAM privilege-escalation path via role trust. None of the intrusive steps triggered an alert, indicating a detection gap in the cloud control plane.

Addressing the four High/Critical findings closes the demonstrated escalation path; the remaining items reduce residual risk and improve detection coverage.

attack_narrative.step: Enumerated tenant and public storage; identified listable bucket
Validated leaked access key; enumerated IAM permissions
Escalated via iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy on a privileged role
Assumed admin role; reached organisation management account

detection_assessment: Control-plane logging was enabled but no alerting fired on the privilege-escalation actions. CloudTrail captured the IAM changes, but there were no detections for AssumeRolePolicy modification or for first-time admin role assumption. Recommended detections are listed under Recommendations.

findings.title: S3 bucket public-access block not enabled
findings.description: All four public-access-block settings are disabled at the bucket level, allowing a misconfigured policy or ACL to expose contents publicly.
findings.attack_path: Bucket has no public-access block → a permissive ACL or policy would make objects world-readable.
findings.evidence:
$ aws s3api get-public-access-block --bucket example-customer-data
{ "PublicAccessBlockConfiguration": { "BlockPublicAcls": false, "IgnorePublicAcls": false, "BlockPublicPolicy": false, "RestrictPublicBuckets": false } }
findings.impact: Potential exposure of personal data; a compliance gap under privacy regulations governing security of processing.
findings.remediation: Enable all four public-access-block settings at both bucket and account level.

findings.title: IAM privilege-escalation path via role trust modification
findings.description: A low-privileged principal holds iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy on a highly privileged role, allowing it to add itself as a trusted principal and assume administrative access.
findings.attack_path: app-deploy has iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy on org-admin → rewrite trust to include app-deploy → sts:AssumeRole into org-admin.
findings.impact: Full escalation from application identity to organisation administrator.
findings.remediation: Remove iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy from application identities; apply permission boundaries to privileged roles.

findings.title: User-assigned managed identity shared across workloads
findings.description: A single user-assigned managed identity is attached to multiple workloads of differing trust levels, widening blast radius if any one workload is compromised.
findings.impact: Compromise of the lowest-trust workload yields the identity's full permission set across all attached workloads.
findings.remediation: Split into per-workload identities scoped to least privilege.

structural: Apply permission boundaries to all privileged roles.
Split shared managed identities into per-workload identities.
strategic: Add control-plane detections for AssumeRolePolicy changes and first-time admin role assumption.
Adopt an organisation-wide guardrail (SCP/Azure Policy) baseline.

appendices.title: A. Tooling
appendices.body: Enumeration performed with read-only tooling; intrusive steps gated through the approval workflow.
